editorial:
Imagine a guy who won the biggest book award in France but spent the rest of his life being bullied by a group of grumpy regulars at a dive bar called Le Renard jaune. That is exactly how this story starts. Charles Senac is basically the town punching bag, and when he turns up dead in his house, you can bet your life that one of those bar flies did it. The vibe is a mix of a classic whodunit and a dark comedy, feeling like a quirky play where everyone has a secret and a reason to hate the victim. It is a small-scale story that focuses on human pettiness and the funny side of crime.

You will probably love how the inspector handles the case, as he treats the investigation like a game of cat and mouse. The acting is great, though the pace slows down a bit in the middle. If you enjoy movies where you can try to guess the killer along with the detective, this is for you.
endingExplained: The mystery wraps up when Inspector Giraud figures out that the murder was not just about hate, but about money and jealousy. Through a series of clever questions, the detective traps the killer among the bar regulars. It turns out that the motives were simpler than they seemed, involving greed and old grudges. The movie ends with a satisfying reveal that shows how the killer's own ego led to their downfall, bringing a funny but just conclusion to the case.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic murder mysteries and eccentric characters.
